docs.text:
Educational & AI-Generated Documentation Disclaimer

This documentation was generated with the assistance of AI and is intended strictly for educational and learning purposes. We are not the original authors or copyright owners of the underlying Caldis library.

Caldis is an acausal, equation-based modeling and simulation platform in Python for thermal and energy systems (such as Brayton gas turbines, Rankine cycles, heat pumps, organic Rankine cycles, cooling loops, and storage vessels).

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Acausal Equation-Oriented Modeling: Components do not compute explicit outputs. Instead, each component defines physical conservation residuals (mass, momentum, energy).
  • Square System Verification (DOF Preflight): Automatically counts equations and variables before solving to prevent under- or over-specified models.
  • CoolProp & Equation of State Integration: Thermodynamic state evaluation keyed on \((p, h)\) across single-phase and two-phase regimes without artificial dome boundaries.
  • Robust Multi-Stage Solvers: Combines damped global Newton solvers, homotopy/continuation algorithms, and rule-based autostart propagation.
  • Dynamic Simulation: Native index-1 DAE integrator supporting thermal masses, compressible volumes, and time-dependent boundary conditions.
  • Built-in Exergy & Diagnostics: Automatic second-law balances (\(X_{\text{in}}\), \(X_{\text{out}}\), \(X_{\text{dest}}\), \(\eta_{\text{II}}\)) and scaled Jacobian conditioning reports.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from caldis.core.system import System
from caldis.components import Compressor, SimpleHeater, FluidBoundary
from caldis.fluids import CoolPropBackend
from caldis.solvers import solve
from caldis.solvers.autostart import fix_port, autostart

# 1. Initialize fluid backend
air = CoolPropBackend("Air")

# 2. Instantiate components
src = FluidBoundary("src", p=1.0e5, T=288.15, mdot=-2.0, backend=air)
comp = Compressor("comp", backend=air, eta_is=0.85)
cooler = SimpleHeater("cooler", backend=air, Qdot=None, dp=0.0)
sink = FluidBoundary("sink", backend=air)

# 3. Assemble system and connect ports
sys = System("air_compression")
sys.add(src, comp, cooler, sink)
sys.connect(src.port, comp.inl)
sys.connect(comp.out, cooler.inl)
sys.connect(cooler.out, sink.port)

# 4. Impose design constraints
fix_port(sys, comp.out, p=6.0e5)      # Target 6 bar discharge
fix_port(sys, cooler.out, T=303.15)   # Target 30 °C outlet

# 5. Automatically seed start values and solve
autostart(sys)
sol = solve(sys)

# 6. Read results
print(f"Compressor shaft power: {comp.Wdot / 1e3:.2f} kW")
print(f"Cooler duty extracted:  {cooler.Qdot / 1e3:.2f} kW")

docs.title: add(*components: Component) -> Tuple[Component, ...]

Registers one or more physical components with the system container.

Parameter Type Description *components Component Arbitrary number of component instances (Compressor, FluidBoundary, etc.).

Returns: The component or tuple of components registered.

docs.title: connect(port_a: FluidPort, port_b: FluidPort, close_loop: bool = False) -> Connection
docs.text:
Creates an acausal connection between two fluid ports.

Parameter Type Default Description port_a FluidPort required First fluid port. port_b FluidPort required Second fluid port. close_loop bool False When True, omits the mass balance equation (\(\dot{m}_a + \dot{m}_b = 0\)) to eliminate linear dependency in closed cycles.

Residuals Generated: - Equality of pressure: \(p_a - p_b = 0\) - Equality of specific enthalpy: \(h_a - h_b = 0\) - Mass conservation (if close_loop=False): \(\dot{m}_a + \dot{m}_b = 0\)

Returns: DOFReport with attributes: - n_unknowns: int: Total number of unknown variables. - n_equations: int: Total number of residual equations. - dof: int: \(N_{\text{unknowns}} - N_{\text{equations}}\). - ok: bool: True if system is square (\(\text{DOF} = 0\)).

docs.title: preflight(system: System, verbose: bool = True, check_start: bool = True, raise_on_fail: bool = False) -> bool
docs.text: Unified pre-solve validator checking DOF, start-point evaluability (preventing CoolProp out-of-domain crashes), and component sanity.

docs.title: Why DOF Verification Matters
docs.text:
In physical systems simulation, one of the most frustrating experiences is encountering a solver failure that simply reports:

Singular matrix in LU factorization

In almost all cases, this is not caused by numerical instability—it is caused by a modeling mismatch: - Under-specified system: Too few boundary conditions or equations specified. For example, a compressor is defined without fixing its discharge pressure, pressure ratio, or mass flow rate. - Over-specified system: Too many constraints applied to the same stream. For example, setting pressure on both the inlet and outlet of a frictionless pipe or fixing both inlet and outlet temperatures on a fixed-duty heater.

Caldis eliminates this ambiguity before invoking the solver using structural DOF preflight.

docs.title: The Preflight Mechanism
docs.text: Before running any Newton iteration or homotopy continuation, solve(sys) and simulate(sys) run preflight(sys).

docs.title: 1. Counting Rule
docs.text:
For a system with components \(C\), connections \(K\), and system constraints \(S\):

\[\text{DOF} = N_{\text{unknowns}} - N_{\text{equations}}\]

where:

\[N_{\text{unknowns}} = \sum_{c \in C} \text{len}(c.\text{all_variables}())\] \[N_{\text{equations}} = \sum_{c \in C} \text{len}(c.\text{residuals}()) + \sum_{k \in K} \text{len}(k.\text{residuals}()) + \text{len}(S)\]

docs.title: 2. DOF Status Classifications
docs.text: DOF Value Status Diagnostic Message Action Required \(\text{DOF} = 0\) Square (OK) [DOF ok] N unknowns, N equations — système carré. Proceed to start check. \(\text{DOF} > 0\) Under-specified [DOF sous-spécifié] N unknowns, M equations : il manque K condition(s)... Add a boundary spec (FluidBoundary) or fix_port. \(\text{DOF} < 0\) Over-specified [DOF sur-spécifié] N unknowns, M equations : K équation(s) de trop... Remove redundant pressure/temperature specs.

docs.title: Using fix_port
docs.text:
The recommended approach to close free degrees of freedom is the fix_port helper:

from caldis.solvers.autostart import fix_port

# Pin pressure and seed start value
fix_port(sys, comp.out, p=6.0e5)

# Pin temperature (converts to enthalpy via port backend)
fix_port(sys, hex.cold_out, T=350.15)

fix_port performs two critical tasks simultaneously: 1. Adds a system residual: \(p_{\text{port}} - p_{\text{target}} = 0\) 2. Seeds port._p.start = p_target with high provenance so autostart knows the value.

docs.title: Arbitrary Constraints
docs.text:
For inter-component relationships (e.g., maintaining a constant pressure ratio or temperature difference):

# Impose pressure ratio: p_out = 4.5 * p_in
sys.add_constraint(
    lambda: comp.out.p - 4.5 * comp.inl.p,
    name="compressor_pressure_ratio"
)

docs.title: Philosophical Foundations
docs.text:
Most process and thermal simulators operate in a causal (input \(\rightarrow\) output) fashion or rely on complex symbolic restructuring (e.g., standard Modelica engines) that often yields cryptic errors like "system structurally singular" when boundary conditions are slightly altered.

Caldis takes an equation-oriented, acausal, residual-based approach:

  1. No component calculates an output: A component does not calculate \(T_{\text{out}}\) given \(T_{\text{in}}\). Instead, it declares equations \(F(x) = 0\) that describe its physical balance laws.
  2. Global System Assembly: The system aggregates all component variables into a single state vector \(x \in \mathbb{R}^n\) and gathers all physical and topological residuals into \(F(x) \in \mathbb{R}^m\).
  3. Multi-Stage Preflight: Prior to invoking nonlinear solvers, the system runs explicit degree-of-freedom checking, evaluability checks, and physical sanity bounds.

docs.title: 1. Variables (Variable)
docs.text: A Variable represents a single scalar unknown in the system: - start: Initial guess for the iterative solver. - value: Current numeric value. - lower / upper: Optional physical bounds (e.g., \(p \ge 0\), \(T \ge 0\)). - scale: Characteristic physical scale used to normalize Jacobian columns. - differential: Flag set to True for dynamic state variables (e.g., mass \(M\), internal energy \(U\), wall temperature \(T_{\text{wall}}\)) which carry a .der attribute (\(\dot{x}\)).

docs.title: 2. Fluid Ports (FluidPort)
docs.text:
Fluid interaction between components occurs via ports. Every FluidPort owns exactly three core variables: - _p: Pressure in Pascals (\(\text{Pa}\)). - _h: Specific enthalpy in Joules per kilogram (\(\text{J/kg}\)). - _mdot: Mass flow rate in kilograms per second (\(\text{kg/s}\)).

Thermodynamic properties (\(T, s, \rho, x\)) are exposed as dynamic read-only properties calculated via the attached FluidBackend.

docs.title: 3. Connections (Connection)
docs.text: When two ports port_a and port_b are connected via sys.connect(port_a, port_b): - Pressure equality: \(p_a - p_b = 0\) - Enthalpy equality: \(h_a - h_b = 0\) - Mass balance: \(\dot{m}_a + \dot{m}_b = 0\) (omitted when close_loop=True).

docs.title: 4. Components (Component)
docs.text: A Component can be a leaf (defining its own residual list) or a composite (embedding child components). It provides: - all_variables(): Recursive list of internal and port variables. - residuals(): Recursive list of equation residuals \(F_i(x)\). - residual_names(): Human-readable diagnostic labels for each equation. - update_outputs(): Calculates post-convergence engineering outputs (power \(\dot{W}\), duty \(\dot{Q}\), pressure ratios, efficiencies). - start_sanity(): Pre-solve checks warning against unphysical start values. - physical_check(): Post-solve checks detecting unphysical converged states (such as temperature crossings in heat exchangers).

docs.title: Sign Conventions & Port Standards
docs.text: Consistent sign conventions are essential for modular energy system simulation. Caldis enforces explicit conventions across all components.

docs.title: Fluid Mass Flow Rates (mdot)
docs.text:
Caldis uses the inlet-positive convention:

\[\dot{m} > 0 \quad \text{enters the component}\] \[\dot{m} < 0 \quad \text{leaves the component}\] 
   Inlet Port                      Outlet Port
   mdot > 0                        mdot < 0
  ───────────> [  Component  ] ───────────>

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
1. Mass Balance across two-port components:

    \[\dot{m}_{\text{in}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\]

  2. Sources and Sinks (FluidBoundary):

    • A fluid source (feeding fluid into the system) sends mass out of its own port, so mdot is negative: 
      src = FluidBoundary("feed", p=3e5, T=293.15, mdot=-1.5, backend=be)
    • A fluid sink (receiving fluid from the system) receives mass into its port, so its resolved mdot will be positive.

  3. Connections: When connecting port_a to port_b:

    \[\dot{m}_a + \dot{m}_b = 0\]

docs.title: Power and Work Conventions (\(\dot{W}\))
docs.text:
Caldis adopts the power producer positive convention:

\[\dot{W} > 0 \quad \text{work produced by the system / component}\] \[\dot{W} < 0 \quad \text{work absorbed by the system / component}\]

Turbine (Turbine):

Delivers shaft work (\(\dot{W}_{\text{turb}} > 0\)):

\[\dot{W}_{\text{turb}} = \eta_{\text{mech}} \cdot \dot{m}_{\text{in}} \cdot (h_{\text{in}} - h_{\text{out}})\]

Compressor (Compressor):

Absorbs electrical or shaft work (reported as \(\dot{W}_{\text{comp}} < 0\)):

\[\dot{W}_{\text{comp}} = - \dot{m}_{\text{in}} \cdot (h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{in}})\]

Net Cycle Power:

\[W_{\text{net}} = \dot{W}_{\text{turbine}} + \dot{W}_{\text{compressor}}\]

docs.title: Thermal Duties (\(\dot{Q}\))
docs.text:
Heat transferred into the fluid stream is positive:

\[\dot{Q} > 0 \quad \text{fluid is heated}\] \[\dot{Q} < 0 \quad \text{fluid is cooled}\]

In SimpleHeater:

\[\dot{Q} = \dot{m}_{\text{in}} \cdot (h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{in}})\]

In SizingHX / RatingHX:

\[\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}} = \dot{m}_{\text{hot}} \cdot (h_{\text{hot,in}} - h_{\text{hot,out}}) > 0 \quad (\text{heat lost by hot stream})\] \[\dot{Q}_{\text{cold}} = \dot{m}_{\text{cold}} \cdot (h_{\text{cold,out}} - h_{\text{cold,in}}) > 0 \quad (\text{heat gained by cold stream})\]

Coupling equation:

\[\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}} - \dot{Q}_{\text{cold}} = 0\]

docs.title: State Coordinate Standard: \((p, h)\)
docs.text: Caldis models all fluid streams using pressure (\(p\)) and specific enthalpy (\(h\)), never \((p, T)\).

docs.title: Why \((p, h)\)?
docs.text: Under the two-phase saturation dome, temperature and pressure are not independent (\(T = T_{\text{sat}}(p)\)). Specifying \((p, T)\) within the dome is ill-posed. In contrast: - Specific enthalpy \(h\) is strictly monotonic across liquid, two-phase, and superheated vapor regions. - Incompressible and compressible regimes are handled uniformly without switching state variables.

docs.title: Start Point & Provenance System
docs.text:
Nonlinear algebraic solvers for thermodynamic cycles are notoriously sensitive to initial guesses (\(x_0\)). An arbitrary initial point can easily cause CoolProp to evaluate properties in two-phase regions with zero flow or unphysical negative temperatures, triggering crashes.

Caldis provides a three-tier start initialization and rule propagation engine (caldis.solvers.autostart).

docs.title: The Provenance Hierarchy
docs.text:
To ensure manual user overrides are never clobbered by automatic propagation, every port variable tracks a provenance level:

0: DEFAULT   <   1: PROPAGATED   <   2: HINT   <   3: BOUNDARY
  • DEFAULT (0): Universal safe baseline initialized by the fluid backend (typically 1 bar, 283.15 K).
  • PROPAGATED (1): Inferred by topological rules (e.g., flow continuity across a valve or heater).
  • HINT (2): Explicitly provided by the user using sys.set_start_port(...) or sys.set_start(...).
  • BOUNDARY (3): Imposed boundary specifications from FluidBoundary or fix_port.

Propagation only writes into a variable if its current state is DEFAULT (0). It will never overwrite a HINT or BOUNDARY.

docs.title: How Autostart Propagation Works
docs.text: autostart(sys, verbose=False) executes a fixpoint loop over direction-agnostic rules until no more variables can be updated:

docs.title: Propagation Rules
docs.text:
1. Connections:
  2. \(p_a \leftrightarrow p_b\)
  3. \(h_a \leftrightarrow h_b\)
  4. \(\dot{m}_a \leftrightarrow -\dot{m}_b\)
  5. Two-Port Components (Valves, Heaters, Turbines, Compressors):
  6. Flow continuity: \(\dot{m}_{\text{in}} = -\dot{m}_{\text{out}}\)
  7. Enthalpy preservation across valves (isenthalpic): \(h_{\text{out}} = h_{\text{in}}\)
  8. Known pressure drops across heaters: \(p_{\text{out}} = p_{\text{in}} - \Delta p\)
  9. Splitters & Mixers:
  10. Splitter: \(p_{\text{out}} = p_{\text{in}}\), \(h_{\text{out}} = h_{\text{in}}\)

docs.title: Manual Seeding Hints
docs.text: When autostart requires guidance (e.g., across machines where enthalpy changes significantly):

docs.title: sys.set_start_port
docs.text:
Sets a start hint on a specific port:

# Sets pressure and converts 450 °C into enthalpy using the port backend
sys.set_start_port(comp.out, p=12.0e5, T=450 + 273.15)

docs.title: sys.set_start
docs.text:
Applies hints across all fluid ports of a component:

# Apply hint to all ports on the cold side of a heat exchanger
sys.set_start(recup, p=10.0e5, T=350.15, side="cold")

docs.title: sys.set_start_internal
docs.text:
Applies initial values to internal discretised variables (such as cell temperatures or wall profiles in HXSim):

sys.set_start_internal(hx_sim, "Tw", 400.0)

docs.title: Common Component Attributes & Lifecycle
docs.text:
Every component inherits from caldis.core.component.Component and participates in the system lifecycle:

  • ports: List of attached FluidPort instances.
  • all_variables(): All internal scalar variables plus port variables.
  • residuals(): Array of residuals evaluated during each solver step.
  • update_outputs(): Evaluates post-solve engineering properties (stored in _outputs and accessed via @property).
  • start_sanity(): Diagnostic checks to warn if the initial start point violates physical constraints.

docs.title: SimpleHeater
docs.text: caldis.components.combustion.heater.SimpleHeater models a thermal duty source or sink on a single fluid stream with optional pressure drop.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
SimpleHeater(name, backend, Qdot=None, dp=0.0, T_source=None)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. backend FluidBackend required — Fluid thermodynamic properties backend. Qdot float or None None \(\text{W}\) Thermal duty. \(\dot{Q} > 0\) heats, \(\dot{Q} < 0\) cools. docs.text:
1. Parameter Mode (Qdot is provided as a float):
  2. \(\dot{Q}\) is fixed as an input parameter in params["Qdot"].
  3. The outlet enthalpy \(h_{\text{out}}\) adapts according to the specified heat duty.
  4. Sizing / Unknown Mode (Qdot=None):
  5. Creates an internal unknown variable self._Qdot (start=0.0, scale=1e3).
  6. The system must provide one closing constraint (e.g., pinning outlet temperature via fix_port(sys, heater.out, T=...)).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort Fluid entry port. out Outlet FluidPort Fluid exit port.

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 3 residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\)$
  2. Pressure relation ("dp"): $\(p_{\text{out}} - (p_{\text{inl}} - \Delta p) = 0\)$
  3. Energy balance ("energy"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{inl}}) - \dot{Q} = 0\)$

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs & Exergy
docs.text:
• heater.Qdot: Current heat duty (\(\text{W}\)).
  • Entropy Generation (heater.entropy_generation()): $\(\dot{S}_{\text{gen}} = \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (s_{\text{out}} - s_{\text{inl}}) - \frac{\dot{Q}}{T_{\text{source}}}\)$ (With \(T_{\text{source}} = \infty\), \(\dot{Q}/T_{\text{source}} = 0\)).
  • Exergy Balance (heater.exergy_balance(T0, p0)): $\(\dot{X}_Q = \dot{Q} \left(1 - \frac{T_0}{T_{\text{source}}}\right)\)$ $\(\Delta \dot{X}_{\text{stream}} = \dot{X}_{\text{out}} - \dot{X}_{\text{inl}}\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{dest}} = \dot{X}_Q - \Delta \dot{X}_{\text{stream}} = T_0 \dot{S}_{\text{gen}}\)$ Note: Returns None if T_source is not configured.

docs.title: System Context: Brayton Gas Turbine Circuit
Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
CombustionChamber(
    name, backend_air, backend_fuel,
    LHV=50.0e6, eta_comb=1.0, dp_rel=0.04,

    T_max_warn=1700.0
)

LHV float 50.0e6 \(\text{J/kg}\) Lower heating value of the fuel (default corresponds to methane). eta_comb float 1.0 — Combustion thermal efficiency (\(0 < \eta_{\text{comb}} \le 1\)). dp_rel float 0.04 — Fractional relative pressure loss (\(\Delta p / p_{\text{air}} = 0.04\)). docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Backend Description air_in Inlet FluidPort backend_air Compressed air inlet port (\(\dot{m} > 0\)). fuel_in Inlet FluidPort backend_fuel Fuel supply inlet port (\(\dot{m} > 0\)). gas_out Outlet FluidPort backend_air Flue gas discharge port (\(\dot{m} < 0\)).

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 3 non-linear algebraic residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{air}} + \dot{m}_{\text{fuel}} + \dot{m}_{\text{gas}} = 0\)$
  2. Pressure drop relation ("pressure"): $\(p_{\text{gas}} - p_{\text{air}} (1 - \Delta p_{\text{rel}}) = 0\)$
  3. Reference-compensated energy balance ("energy"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{air}} (h_{\text{air}} - h_{a,\text{ref}}) + \dot{m}_{\text{fuel}} \left(h_{\text{fuel}} - h_{f,\text{ref}} + \eta_{\text{comb}} \cdot \text{LHV}\right) + \dot{m}_{\text{gas}} (h_{\text{gas}} - h_{a,\text{ref}}) = 0\)$

where: - \(h_{a,\text{ref}} = h(p_{\text{ref}}, T_{\text{ref}})\) evaluated in backend_air. - \(h_{f,\text{ref}} = h(p_{\text{ref}}, T_{\text{ref}})\) evaluated in backend_fuel. - Referencing to \((T_{\text{ref}}, p_{\text{ref}})\) cancels out arbitrary reference state enthalpy offsets between the two property backends.

docs.text:
Updated upon convergence via update_outputs():

Property Symbol Type / Units Formulation comb.Qdot_fuel \(\dot{Q}_{\text{fuel}}\) float (\(\text{W}\)) Total fuel chemical thermal input: \(\dot{m}_{\text{fuel}} \cdot \text{LHV}\). comb.Qdot_released \(\dot{Q}_{\text{released}}\) float (\(\text{W}\)) Net heat released into gas: \(\dot{m}_{\text{fuel}} \cdot \text{LHV} \cdot \eta_{\text{comb}}\). comb.AFR \(\text{AFR}\) float Actual air-to-fuel mass ratio: \(\dot{m}_{\text{air}} / \dot{m}_{\text{fuel}}\). comb.excess_air \(\lambda\) float Excess air coefficient: \(\text{AFR} / \text{AFR}_{\text{stoich}}\).

docs.text:
• \(\dot{m}_{\text{air}} > 0\) and \(\dot{m}_{\text{fuel}} > 0\).
  • \(T_{\text{gas}} > T_{\text{air}}\) (verifies positive combustion temperature rise).
  • \(\lambda > 1.0\) (warns if fuel mixture is rich, as gas turbines operate lean).
  • \(T_{\text{gas}} < T_{\text{max\_warn}}\) (warns if flame or TIT exceeds metallurgical limits).

docs.title: Heat Exchangers
docs.text: Caldis provides both single-zone lumped models (SizingHX, RatingHX) for steady-state sizing and rating design, and a full 1D discretized finite-volume model (HXSim) for dynamic, transient, and two-phase simulations.

docs.title: SizingHX (Heat Exchanger Sizing)
docs.text: caldis.components.HEX.heat_exchanger.SizingHX sizes the required heat transfer area and overall thermal conductance for a given duty. It uses a single-zone regularized log-mean temperature difference (LMTD) formulation.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
Coupling & Energy Balance:

\[\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}} = \dot{m}_{\text{hot}} (h_{\text{hot,in}} - h_{\text{hot,out}})\] \[\dot{Q}_{\text{cold}} = \dot{m}_{\text{cold}} (h_{\text{cold,out}} - h_{\text{cold,in}})\] \[\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}} + \dot{Q}_{\text{cold}} = 0\]

LMTD & Conductance (\(UA\)):

\[\Delta T_1 = T_{\text{hot,in}} - T_{\text{cold,out}}, \quad \Delta T_2 = T_{\text{hot,out}} - T_{\text{cold,in}}\] \[\text{LMTD} = \frac{\Delta T_1 - \Delta T_2}{\ln(\Delta T_1 / \Delta T_2)}\] \[UA = \frac{|\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}}|}{\text{LMTD}}\]

Film Resistance & Sizing Area:

\[U_{\text{overall,hot}} = \left(\frac{1}{h_{\text{hot}}} + \frac{1}{\text{area\_ratio} \cdot h_{\text{cold}}}\right)^{-1}\] \[A_{\text{hot}} = \frac{UA}{U_{\text{overall,hot}}}, \quad A_{\text{cold}} = \text{area\_ratio} \cdot A_{\text{hot}}, \quad A_{\text{total}} = A_{\text{hot}} + A_{\text{cold}}\]

docs.title: Constructor Arguments
docs.text:
SizingHX(
    name,
    backend_hot,
    backend_cold,
    h_hot,
    h_cold,
    area_ratio_cold_to_hot
)
- name (str): Unique component identifier. - backend_hot (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the hot channel. - backend_cold (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the cold channel. - h_hot (float): Hot-side convective film coefficient [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. - h_cold (float): Cold-side convective film coefficient [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. - area_ratio_cold_to_hot (float): Ratio of cold-side to hot-side surface area \(A_{\text{cold}} / A_{\text{hot}}\) (\(\ge 1\) for cold-side finned, \(= 1\) for bare plate/tube).

docs.title: Ports (Inputs / Boundary Interfaces)
docs.text:
• hot_in: Hot stream inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • hot_out: Hot stream outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • cold_in: Cold stream inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).
  • cold_out: Cold stream outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).

docs.title: Internal Variables (Solved by System)
docs.text:
• UA: Overall thermal conductance [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)].
  • A_hot: Required heat transfer area on the hot side [\(\text{m}^2\)].

docs.title: Outputs (Post-Solve Properties)
docs.text:
• hx.UA (float): Solved overall conductance [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)].
  • hx.A_hot (float): Sized hot-side area [\(\text{m}^2\)].
  • hx.A_cold (float): Sized cold-side area [\(\text{m}^2\)].
  • hx.A_total (float): Total heat transfer area \(A_{\text{hot}} + A_{\text{cold}}\) [\(\text{m}^2\)].
  • hx.U_overall_hot (float): Overall heat transfer coefficient referenced to \(A_{\text{hot}}\) [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)].
  • hx.U_overall_cold (float): Overall heat transfer coefficient referenced to \(A_{\text{cold}}\) [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)].
  • hx.Qdot (float): Heat transfer rate \(\dot{Q}_{\text{hot}}\) [\(\text{W}\)].
  • hx.DTLM (float): Log-mean temperature difference [\(\text{K}\)].

docs.title: Sanity & Physical Checks
docs.text:
• Checks that the hot stream is warmer than the cold stream (\(T_{\text{hot,in}} \ge T_{\text{cold,out}}\) and \(T_{\text{hot,out}} \ge T_{\text{cold,in}}\)).
  • Detects temperature pinches/crosses (\(\Delta T_1 \cdot \Delta T_2 > 0\)).
  • Warns against degenerate inlet/outlet temperature differences.

docs.title: RatingHX (Heat Exchanger Rating)
docs.text: caldis.components.HEX.heat_exchanger.RatingHX evaluates off-design performance when geometry and heat transfer area (or conductance) are fixed. It employs an explicit effectiveness-NTU (\(\varepsilon\text{-NTU}\)) closure.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
Capacity Rates & NTU:

\[C_{\text{hot}} = |\dot{m}_{\text{hot}}| \cdot c_{p,\text{hot}}, \quad C_{\text{cold}} = |\dot{m}_{\text{cold}}| \cdot c_{p,\text{cold}}\] \[C_{\text{min}} = \min(C_{\text{hot}}, C_{\text{cold}}), \quad C_{\text{max}} = \max(C_{\text{hot}}, C_{\text{cold}}), \quad C_r = \frac{C_{\text{min}}}{C_{\text{max}}}\] \[\text{NTU} = \frac{UA}{C_{\text{min}}}\]

Effectiveness (\(\varepsilon\)):

  • Counterflow: $\(\varepsilon = \frac{1 - \exp(-\text{NTU}(1 - C_r))}{1 - C_r \exp(-\text{NTU}(1 - C_r))} \quad (\text{or } \frac{\text{NTU}}{1 + \text{NTU}} \text{ when } C_r \to 1)\)$
  • Coflow (Parallel flow): $\(\varepsilon = \frac{1 - \exp(-\text{NTU}(1 + C_r))}{1 + C_r}\)$

Heat Duty & Energy Balance:

\[\dot{Q} = \varepsilon \cdot C_{\text{min}} \cdot (T_{\text{hot,in}} - T_{\text{cold,in}})\] \[\dot{m}_{\text{hot}} (h_{\text{hot,in}} - h_{\text{hot,out}}) = \dot{Q}\] \[\dot{m}_{\text{cold}} (h_{\text{cold,out}} - h_{\text{cold,in}}) = \dot{Q}\]

docs.title: Constructor Arguments
docs.text:
Provide either UA directly, or the complete physical geometry set (h_hot, h_cold, area_ratio_cold_to_hot, A_hot):

RatingHX(
    name,
    backend_hot,
    backend_cold,
    UA=None,
    h_hot=None,
    h_cold=None,
    area_ratio_cold_to_hot=None,
    A_hot=None,
    flow_config="counterflow"
)
- name (str): Unique component identifier. - backend_hot (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the hot channel. - backend_cold (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the cold channel. - UA (float, optional): Direct overall thermal conductance [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)]. - h_hot (float, optional): Hot-side convective film coefficient [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. - h_cold (float, optional): Cold-side convective film coefficient [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. - area_ratio_cold_to_hot (float, optional): Ratio \(A_{\text{cold}} / A_{\text{hot}}\). - A_hot (float, optional): Fixed hot-side heat transfer area [\(\text{m}^2\)]. - flow_config (str, optional): Flow arrangement, either "counterflow" (default) or "coflow".

docs.title: Ports (Inputs / Boundary Interfaces)
docs.text:
• hot_in: Hot stream inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • hot_out: Hot stream outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • cold_in: Cold stream inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).
  • cold_out: Cold stream outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).

docs.title: Outputs (Post-Solve Properties)
docs.text:
• hx.Qdot (float): Transferred thermal power \(\dot{Q}\) [\(\text{W}\)].
  • hx.effectiveness (float): Heat exchanger thermal effectiveness \(\varepsilon \in [0, 1]\).
  • hx.NTU (float): Number of transfer units.
  • hx.Cr (float): Heat capacity rate ratio \(C_{\text{min}} / C_{\text{max}}\).
  • hx.C_hot (float): Hot fluid capacity rate \(|\dot{m}_{\text{hot}}| \cdot c_{p,\text{hot}}\) [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)].
  • hx.C_cold (float): Cold fluid capacity rate \(|\dot{m}_{\text{cold}}| \cdot c_{p,\text{cold}}\) [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)].
  • hx.UA (float): Conductance applied in rating [\(\text{W}/\text{K}\)].
  • hx.T_hot_out (float): Computed hot-side discharge temperature [\(\text{K}\)].
  • hx.T_cold_out (float): Computed cold-side discharge temperature [\(\text{K}\)].

docs.title: Scope & Constraints
docs.text:
• Valid for single-phase (sensible) heat exchange (constant \(c_p\) evaluated at inlets).
  • Pressure drop is neglected (\(p_{\text{out}} = p_{\text{in}}\)). For condensing, evaporating, or distributed pressure drops, use SizingHX or HXSim.

docs.title: HXSim (Discretized Finite-Volume Heat Exchanger)
docs.text: caldis.components.HEX.hex_discretized.HXSim models a 1D discretized counterflow or coflow heat exchanger with \(N\) elements for steady-state, transient dynamic, and two-phase simulations.

docs.title: Physics & Formulation
docs.text:
• Staggered finite-volume grid:
  • Per cell \(i \in [0, N-1]\):
    • Mass differential state: \(\frac{dM_i}{dt} = \dot{m}_{\text{in}, i} - \dot{m}_{\text{out}, i}\)
    • Energy differential state: \(\frac{dU_i}{dt} = \dot{m}_{\text{in}, i} h_{\text{in}, i} - \dot{m}_{\text{out}, i} h_{\text{out}, i} + \dot{Q}_i\)
    • Algebraic equation of state: \(M_i = \rho_{\text{eff}, i} V_i\), and \(U_i = V_i (\rho h_{\text{eff}, i} - p_i)\)
  • Per element wall:
    • Transient wall temperature: \(m_{\text{wall}, i} c_{p,\text{wall}} \frac{dT_{\text{wall}, i}}{dt} = \dot{Q}_{\text{hot}\to\text{wall}, i} + \dot{Q}_{\text{cold}\to\text{wall}, i}\)
  • Per internal cell face \(k \in [0, N-2]\):
    • Momentum equation: \(p_k - p_{k+1} = \left(\frac{dp}{dz}\right)_k \Delta L_k\)
  • Replaceable correlation bricks:
  • Convection, radiation, pressure gradient (\(dp/dz\)), and two-phase void fraction (\(\varepsilon\)).

docs.title: Constructor Arguments
docs.text:
HXSim(
    name,
    backend_hot,
    backend_cold,
    n_elements=10,
    flow_config="counterflow",
    geometry_params=None,
    m_wall=1.0,
    cp_wall=500.0,
    R_fouling=0.0,
    geometry_fn=None,
    h_conv_hot=None,
    h_conv_cold=None,
    h_rad_hot=None,
    h_rad_cold=None,
    dp_hot=None,
    dp_cold=None,
    void_hot=None,
    void_cold=None
)
- name (str): Unique component identifier. - backend_hot (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the hot channel. - backend_cold (FluidBackend): Fluid property backend for the cold channel. - n_elements (int, optional): Number of spatial finite-volume discretization elements along the length. Default is 10. - flow_config (str, optional): Flow configuration, "counterflow" (default) or "coflow". - geometry_params (dict, optional): Channel and surface geometry dictionary passed to geometry_fn. Typical keys for default plate: - plate_width (float): Channel width in meters (default: 0.1 m). - plate_gap (float): Channel plate gap/spacing in meters (default: 0.003 m). - L_total (float): Total heat exchanger length in meters (default: 0.5 m). - m_wall (float, optional): Total thermal mass of the separating wall [\(\text{kg}\)]. Default is 1.0. - cp_wall (float, optional): Specific heat capacity of the wall material [\(\text{J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\)]. Default is 500.0. - R_fouling (float, optional): Thermal fouling resistance [\((\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})/\text{W}\)]. Default is 0.0. - geometry_fn (callable, optional): Function (element_index, geometry_params) -> dict returning geometry metrics (A_exchange, A_cross, V_internal, dh, perimeter_wet, L_elem). Defaults to geometry_plate. - h_conv_hot, h_conv_cold (callable, optional): Convective heat transfer brick brick(ctx) -> h_conv [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. Defaults to h_conv_constant(500.0). - h_rad_hot, h_rad_cold (callable, optional): Radiative equivalent heat transfer brick brick(ctx) -> h_rad [\(\text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\)]. Defaults to h_rad_constant(0.0). - dp_hot, dp_cold (callable, optional): Frictional pressure gradient brick brick(ctx) -> dp/dz [\(\text{Pa}/\text{m}\)]. Defaults to dp_linear(1000.0). - void_hot, void_cold (callable, optional): Two-phase void fraction brick brick(ctx) -> eps \(\in [0, 1]\). Defaults to void_homogeneous().

docs.title: Ports (Inputs / Boundary Interfaces)
docs.text:
• hot_in: Hot channel inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • hot_out: Hot channel outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_hot).
  • cold_in: Cold channel inlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).
  • cold_out: Cold channel outlet port (FluidPort, backend: backend_cold).

docs.title: Internal Solved States & Variables
docs.text:
• Hot side per element: mass hold-up \(M_{h, i}\), internal energy \(U_{h, i}\), pressure \(p_{h, i}\), enthalpy \(h_{h, i}\).
  • Cold side per element: mass hold-up \(M_{c, i}\), internal energy \(U_{c, i}\), pressure \(p_{c, i}\), enthalpy \(h_{c, i}\).
  • Wall per element: wall temperature \(T_{w, i}\).
  • Internal face flows: \(\dot{m}_{fh, k}\) and \(\dot{m}_{fc, k}\) for \(k \in [0, N-2]\).

  • hx.T_cold (list[float]): Array of temperatures along the cold stream cells [\(\text{K}\)].
  • hx.Tw (list[float]): Array of wall temperatures along each element [\(\text{K}\)].

docs.title: Turbomachinery: Compressor & Turbine
docs.text: Turbomachinery components model fluid work interactions with constant isentropic and mechanical efficiencies.

docs.title: Compressor
docs.text: caldis.components.machines.compressor.Compressor models a steady-state adiabatic compressor.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
Compressor(name, backend, eta_is)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Unique identifier string for the component. backend FluidBackend required — Fluid thermodynamic properties backend. eta_is float required — Isentropic efficiency (\(0 < \eta_{\text{is}} \le 1\)). Divides the isentropic enthalpy rise.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort Fluid suction / inlet port. out Outlet FluidPort Fluid discharge / outlet port.

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 2 non-linear algebraic residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\)$
  2. Isentropic compression relation ("isentropic"): $\(h_{\text{out}} - \left( h_{\text{inl}} + \frac{h_{\text{out}, s} - h_{\text{inl}}}{\eta_{\text{is}}} \right) = 0\)$

where: - \(s_{\text{inl}} = s(p_{\text{inl}}, h_{\text{inl}})\) - \(h_{\text{out}, s} = h(p_{\text{out}}, s_{\text{inl}})\) evaluated via backend.h_ps(self.out.p, s_in).

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs & Properties
docs.text:
Updated upon solver convergence via update_outputs():

Property Symbol Type / Units Description comp.Wdot \(\dot{W}\) float (\(\text{W}\)) Shaft power absorbed by the compressor. Follows thermodynamic sign convention (\(\dot{W} < 0\) for work done on fluid): \(\dot{W} = -\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{inl}})\). comp.pressure_ratio \(\Pi\) float Pressure ratio: \(p_{\text{out}} / p_{\text{inl}}\).

docs.title: Exergy Balance
docs.text: Evaluated via comp.exergy_balance(T0, p0): $\(\dot{X}_{\text{in}} = \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} \cdot e_{x}(p_{\text{inl}}, h_{\text{inl}}; T_0, p_0)\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{out}} = \dot{m}_{\text{out}} \cdot e_{x}(p_{\text{out}}, h_{\text{out}}; T_0, p_0)\)$ $\(\dot{W}_{\text{absorbed}} = |\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{inl}})|\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{dest}} = \dot{W}_{\text{absorbed}} - (\dot{X}_{\text{out}} - \dot{X}_{\text{in}})\)$

docs.title: Pre-Solve Sanity Checks (_own_start_sanity)
docs.text: Prior to system solving, Compressor validates: - Pressure Gradient: \(p_{\text{out}} > p_{\text{inl}}\). Warns or fails if initial conditions specify expansion through the compressor.

docs.title: Turbine
docs.text: caldis.components.machines.turbine.Turbine models an adiabatic expansion turbine.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
Turbine(name, backend, eta_is=0.89, eta_mech=1.0)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Unique identifier string for the component. backend FluidBackend required — Fluid thermodynamic properties backend. eta_is float 0.89 — Isentropic expansion efficiency (\(0 < \eta_{\text{is}} \le 1\)). Multiplies the isentropic drop. eta_mech float 1.0 — Mechanical shaft efficiency (\(0 < \eta_{\text{mech}} \le 1\)). Accounts for mechanical bearing/windage losses in delivered shaft power.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort High-pressure turbine inlet / admission port. out Outlet FluidPort Low-pressure turbine exhaust port.

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 2 non-linear algebraic residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\)$
  2. Expansion enthalpy equation ("isentropic"): $\(h_{\text{out}} - \left[ h_{\text{inl}} - \eta_{\text{is}} \cdot (h_{\text{inl}} - h_{\text{out}, s}) \right] = 0\)$

where: - \(s_{\text{inl}} = s(p_{\text{inl}}, h_{\text{inl}})\) - \(h_{\text{out}, s} = h(p_{\text{out}}, s_{\text{inl}})\) evaluated via backend.h_ps(self.out.p, s_in).

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs & Properties
docs.text:
Updated upon solver convergence via update_outputs():

Property Symbol Type / Units Description turb.Wdot \(\dot{W}\) float (\(\text{W}\)) Net mechanical shaft power delivered (\(\dot{W} > 0\)): \(\dot{W} = \eta_{\text{mech}} \cdot \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{inl}} - h_{\text{out}})\). turb.Wdot_is \(\dot{W}_{\text{is}}\) float (\(\text{W}\)) Maximum theoretical isentropic shaft power: \(\dot{W}_{\text{is}} = \eta_{\text{mech}} \cdot \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{inl}} - h_{\text{out}, s})\). turb.pressure_ratio \(\Pi\) float Expansion pressure ratio: \(p_{\text{inl}} / p_{\text{out}}\). turb.h_out_s \(h_{\text{out}, s}\) float (\(\text{J/kg}\)) Ideal isentropic discharge specific enthalpy. turb.T_out_s \(T_{\text{out}, s}\) float (\(\text{K}\)) Ideal isentropic discharge temperature: \(T(p_{\text{out}}, h_{\text{out}, s})\).

docs.title: Exergy Balance
docs.text: Evaluated via turb.exergy_balance(T0, p0): $\(\dot{X}_{\text{in}} = \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} \cdot e_{x}(p_{\text{inl}}, h_{\text{inl}}; T_0, p_0)\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{out}} = \dot{m}_{\text{out}} \cdot e_{x}(p_{\text{out}}, h_{\text{out}}; T_0, p_0)\)$ $\(\dot{W}_{\text{shaft}} = \eta_{\text{mech}} \cdot \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (h_{\text{inl}} - h_{\text{out}})\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{dest}} = (\dot{X}_{\text{in}} - \dot{X}_{\text{out}}) - \dot{W}_{\text{shaft}}\)$

docs.title: Pre-Solve Sanity Checks (_own_start_sanity)
docs.text: Validates turbine start conditions before solving: - Pressure drop direction: \(p_{\text{out}} < p_{\text{inl}}\) (expansion requirement). - Inlet mass flow: \(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} > 0\). - High temperature check: \(T_{\text{inl}} > 500\text{ K}\) (warns if start state seems too cold for high-temperature turbines).

docs.title: Boundaries & Sources
docs.text: caldis.components.sources.boundary.FluidBoundary specifies boundary conditions and closes mass/energy streams in thermodynamic network models.

docs.title: FluidBoundary
docs.text: The component fixes thermodynamic intensive state properties \((p, T, h)\) and/or extensive throughput (\(\dot{m}\)) at system boundaries.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
FluidBoundary(name, p=None, T=None, h=None, mdot=None, backend=None)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. p float or None None \(\text{Pa}\) Imposed boundary pressure. T float or None None \(\text{K}\) Imposed boundary temperature. Requires backend. h float or None None \(\text{J/kg}\) Imposed boundary specific enthalpy. Requires backend. mdot float or None None \(\text{kg/s}\) Imposed mass flow rate. Sign convention: \(\dot{m} < 0\) represents fluid leaving the boundary and entering the system; \(\dot{m} > 0\) represents fluid entering the boundary from the system. backend FluidBackend or None None — Thermodynamic fluid property backend. Mandatory if either T or h is provided.

docs.title: Constraints & Validation Rules
docs.text:
• State Over-specification Constraint: At most two of \((p, T, h)\) may be specified. If more than two are provided, a ValueError is raised (at most two of (p, T, h) may be imposed).
  • Backend Requirement: If T or h is specified, backend must not be None, otherwise ValueError is raised.
  • Specification Duality: Any parameter provided is added to params["specs"] and formulated as an equality constraint equation. Any omitted parameter remains free and is determined by downstream system impedance and conservation balances.

docs.title: Ports & Internal Variables
docs.text:
Port Name Direction Type Description port Bidirectional FluidPort Fluid connection port exposing state variables port.p, port.h, port.mdot, and computed port.T.

Fluid-aware start values (port._p.start, port._mdot.start, port._h.start) are automatically initialized from specified parameters upon creation. If both p and T are provided, port._h.start is initialized using backend.h_pt(p, T).

docs.title: Governing Residual Equations
docs.text:
Each imposed specification adds one residual equation to residuals() (with matching identifiers in residual_names()):

Specification Residual Name Residual Formulation Notes p "p" \(p_{\text{port}} - p_{\text{spec}} = 0\) Direct pressure pinning. mdot "mdot" \(\dot{m}_{\text{port}} - \dot{m}_{\text{spec}} = 0\) Direct flow rate constraint. h "h" \(h_{\text{port}} - h_{\text{spec}} = 0\) Enthalpy pinning. T "T" \(h(p_{\text{port}}, T_{\text{spec}}) - h_{\text{port}} = 0\) Evaluated robustly via backend.h_pt(p, T_spec) on current port pressure.

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs
docs.text: FluidBoundary exposes no separate outputs via _outputs. State variables and properties are accessed directly on its port: - boundary.port.p - boundary.port.h - boundary.port.mdot - boundary.port.T

docs.title: 1. Inflow Source (Fully Imposed)
docs.text:
Fluid entering a cycle at 3 bar, 40 °C, and 2 kg/s (\(\dot{m} = -2\text{ kg/s}\)): 

src = FluidBoundary("feed", p=3.0e5, T=313.15, mdot=-2.0, backend=be)

docs.title: 2. Discharge Sink (Pressure Pinned)
docs.text:
Exhaust discharging to atmospheric pressure; mass flow rate and enthalpy are dictated by upstream cycle dynamics: 

sink = FluidBoundary("exhaust", p=1.01325e5, backend=be)

docs.title: 3. Floating-Pressure Flow Source
docs.text:
Inlet where mass flow and temperature are fixed, while source pressure adapts to flow resistance: 

inlet = FluidBoundary("inlet", T=293.15, mdot=-0.5, backend=be)

docs.title: 4. Bare Floating Sink
docs.text:
Closes a stream loop without imposing pressure, enthalpy, or mass flow: 

bare_sink = FluidBoundary("sink", backend=be)

docs.title: Valves & Pressure Restrictions
docs.text: caldis.components.valves.valve.Valve models an adiabatic, isenthalpic expansion valve, throttle, or hydraulic flow restriction.

docs.title: Valve
docs.text: Models flow rate as a function of differential pressure \(\Delta p = p_{\text{inl}} - p_{\text{out}}\) with isenthalpic expansion (\(h_{\text{out}} = h_{\text{inl}}\)).

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
Valve(name, Kv=None, backend=None, flow_law="quadratic", eps=1e-9)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. Kv float or None None Law-dependent Valve flow conductance coefficient. If float, fixed simulation mode is used. If None, valve sizing mode is triggered. backend FluidBackend or None None — Optional fluid thermodynamic backend. flow_law str "quadratic" — Flow regime law: "quadratic" or "linear". Raises ValueError for any other value. eps float 1e-9 \(\text{Pa}\) Smoothing regularization parameter avoiding singular Jacobians at zero pressure drop (\(\Delta p \to 0\)).

docs.title: Operating Modes & Unknowns
docs.text:
• Simulation Mode (Kv given as a number):
  • \(K_v\) is saved in params["Kv"].
  • The mass flow rate is determined algebraically by the imposed pressure drop across the component.
  • Sizing Mode (Kv=None):
  • Sets self.sizing = True and instantiates an internal unknown Variable: $\(\text{self.\_Kv\_var} = \text{Variable}("Kv", \text{start}=10^{-4}, \text{lower}=0.0, \text{scale}=10^{-4})\)$
  • The system must provide a closing equation elsewhere (such as fixing stream mass flow rate or outlet pressure) to calculate the required valve opening.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort Upstream high-pressure entry port. out Outlet FluidPort Downstream throttled discharge port.

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 3 non-linear residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\)$
  2. Hydraulic flow law ("flow_law"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} - \dot{m}_{\text{law}} = 0\)$ where \(\dot{m}_{\text{law}}\) depends on flow_law:
  3. "quadratic" (Turbulent orifice flow): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{law}} = K_v \cdot \text{sgn}(\Delta p) \sqrt{|\Delta p| + \varepsilon}\)$ Units of \(K_v\): \(\text{kg} \cdot \text{s}^{-1} \cdot \text{Pa}^{-0.5}\).
  4. "linear" (Laminar / smoothed flow for stiff initializations): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{law}} = K_v \cdot \Delta p\)$ Units of \(K_v\): \(\text{kg} \cdot \text{s}^{-1} \cdot \text{Pa}^{-1}\).
  5. Isenthalpic expansion ("isenthalpic"): $\(h_{\text{out}} - h_{\text{inl}} = 0\)$

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs & Properties
docs.text:
Updated upon solver convergence via update_outputs():

Property Symbol Type / Units Description valve.Kv \(K_v\) float Conductance coefficient (either parameter value or solved unknown). valve.dp \(\Delta p\) float (\(\text{Pa}\)) Differential pressure drop: \(p_{\text{inl}} - p_{\text{out}}\).

docs.title: Exergy Balance & Dissipation
docs.text: Evaluated via valve.exergy_balance(T0, p0): Throttling is an unrecoverable, purely dissipative process: $\(\dot{S}_{\text{gen}} = \dot{m}_{\text{inl}} (s_{\text{out}} - s_{\text{inl}})\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{dest}} = T_0 \dot{S}_{\text{gen}}\)$ $\(\dot{X}_{\text{supplied}} = \dot{X}_{\text{dest}}, \quad \dot{X}_{\text{recovered}} = 0.0\)$

docs.title: Pre-Solve Sanity Checks (_own_start_sanity)
docs.text: • Validates flow direction impedance: \(p_{\text{inl}} \ge p_{\text{out}}\) (warns if start state specifies negative pressure drop across the valve).

docs.title: Vessels, Tanks & Storage
docs.text: 0-D dynamic fluid control volumes, composite storage tanks with wall thermal mass, lumped thermal capacitances, and phase separators.

docs.title: ControlVolume
docs.text: caldis.components.vessels.control_volume.ControlVolume models a rigid, constant-volume 0-D transient fluid vessel.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
ControlVolume(name, backend, V, p_init, h_init, Qdot=0.0)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. backend FluidBackend required — Fluid thermodynamic properties backend. V float required \(\text{m}^3\) Constant geometric volume (\(V > 0\)). p_init float required \(\text{Pa}\) Initial pressure for variable initialization and density evaluation. h_init float required \(\text{J/kg}\) Initial specific enthalpy for variable initialization. Qdot float 0.0 \(\text{W}\) External thermal heat flow into the control volume (\(\dot{Q} > 0\) heating).

docs.title: Internal Variables & States
docs.text:
• Differential States:
  • _M: Total mass inventory (\(M\)), initialized to \(M_0 = V \cdot \rho(p_{\text{init}}, h_{\text{init}})\).
  • _U: Total internal energy (\(U\)), initialized to \(U_0 = V \cdot (\rho_0 h_{\text{init}} - p_{\text{init}})\).
  • Algebraic Variables:
  • _p: Fluid volume pressure (\(p\)), bounded below by \(0.0\).
  • _h: Fluid volume specific enthalpy (\(h\)).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort Fluid admission port (\(p_{\text{inl}} = p\)). out Outlet FluidPort Fluid discharge port (\(p_{\text{out}} = p\), \(h_{\text{out}} = h\)).

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component defines 7 algebraic-differential residuals (residuals()):

Index Residual Name Equation 1 "mass_dyn" \(\frac{dM}{dt} - (\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}}) = 0\) 2 "energy_dyn" \(\frac{dU}{dt} - (\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} h_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} h_{\text{out}} + \dot{Q}) = 0\) 3 "M_def" \(M - V \cdot \rho(p, h) = 0\) 4 "U_def" \(U - V \cdot (\rho(p, h) \cdot h - p) = 0\) 5 "inl_p" \(p_{\text{inl}} - p = 0\) 6 "out_p" \(p_{\text{out}} - p = 0\) 7 "out_h" \(h_{\text{out}} - h = 0\)

docs.title: Outputs & State Properties
docs.text:
• Direct state properties: cv.M (\(\text{kg}\)), cv.U (\(\text{J}\)), cv.p (\(\text{Pa}\)), cv.h (\(\text{J/kg}\)).
  • Updated outputs (cv.update_outputs()):
  • cv.rho: Fluid density (\(\text{kg/m}^3\)).
  • cv.T: Fluid temperature (\(\text{K}\)).
  • cv.x: Vapor quality (\(-1.0\) if subcooled liquid, \(2.0\) if superheated vapor).

docs.title: ControlVolumeP
docs.text: caldis.components.vessels.tank.ControlVolumeP is the constant-pressure (variable-volume) counterpart of ControlVolume (e.g. accumulator or expanding bladder).

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
ControlVolumeP(name, backend, p, h_init, V_init, Qdot=0.0)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. backend FluidBackend required — Fluid thermodynamic properties backend. p float required \(\text{Pa}\) Imposed constant operating pressure. h_init float required \(\text{J/kg}\) Initial fluid specific enthalpy. V_init float required \(\text{m}^3\) Initial volume of the accumulator. Qdot float 0.0 \(\text{W}\) Prescribed external thermal heat addition.

docs.title: Internal Variables & Residuals
docs.text:
• Differential States: _M (\(\text{kg}\)) and _U (\(\text{J}\)).
  • Algebraic Variables: _V (\(\text{m}^3\), breathes to maintain pressure \(p\)) and _h (\(\text{J/kg}\)).
  • Residuals (7): "mass_dyn", "energy_dyn", "M_def", "U_def", "inl_p", "out_p", "out_h".
  • Properties: cv.M, cv.U, cv.V, cv.h, cv.p (fixed parameter), cv.T, cv.rho, cv.x, cv.V_out.

docs.title: ThermalMass
docs.text: caldis.components.vessels.thermal_mass.ThermalMass models a lumped 0-D solid thermal capacitance.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
ThermalMass(name, C, UA, T_init, T_env=None, Qdot_ext=0.0)
Parameter Type Default Units Description & Constraints name str required — Component identifier string. C float required \(\text{J/K}\) Total heat capacity (\(C = m \cdot c_p\)). UA float required \(\text{W/K}\) Thermal conductance to environment. T_init float required \(\text{K}\) Initial body temperature. T_env float or None None \(\text{K}\) Ambient environmental temperature (defaults to T_init). Qdot_ext float 0.0 \(\text{W}\) External thermal power input.

docs.text:
1 differential state _T (\(\text{K}\)): $\(C \frac{dT}{dt} - [UA (T_{\text{env}} - T) + \dot{Q}_{\text{ext}}] = 0 \quad (\text{"energy"})\)$

  • Property: tm.T (\(\text{K}\)).

docs.text: Composite storage systems coupling fluid volumes with container wall thermal masses.

TankConstV(name, backend, V, p_init, h_init, C_wall, T_wall_init, UA_wall, Q_heater=0.0)
TankConstP(name, backend, p, h_init, V_init, C_wall, T_wall_init, UA_wall, Q_heater=0.0)

V / p \(\text{m}^3\) / \(\text{Pa}\) Fixed volume for TankConstV; fixed pressure for TankConstP. p_init / V_init \(\text{Pa}\) / \(\text{m}^3\) Initial state for the free conjugate variable. h_init \(\text{J/kg}\) Initial fluid specific enthalpy. docs.title: Coupling Mechanism
docs.text: Every iteration during _own_residuals(): $\(\dot{Q}_{\text{wall}\to\text{fluid}} = UA_{\text{wall}} \cdot (T_{\text{wall}} - T_{\text{fluid}})\)$ - Fluid volume receives \(\dot{Q}_{\text{fluid}} = \dot{Q}_{\text{wall}\to\text{fluid}}\). - Wall receives \(\dot{Q}_{\text{ext}} = \dot{Q}_{\text{heater}} - \dot{Q}_{\text{wall}\to\text{fluid}}\).

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs
docs.text:
• tank.Q: Current heat transfer from wall to fluid (\(\text{W}\)).
  • tank.T_fluid: Bulk fluid temperature (\(\text{K}\)).
  • tank.T_wall: Wall temperature (\(\text{K}\)).
  • tank.V: Live fluid volume in TankConstP (\(\text{m}^3\)).
  • tank.exergy_balance(T0, p0) returns None (storage systems have no steady-state product).

docs.title: FlashTank
docs.text: caldis.components.vessels.flash_tank.FlashTank models a steady-state adiabatic flash separator operating at isobaric equilibrium.

docs.title: Constructor & Parameters
docs.text:
FlashTank(name, backend)
Parameter Type Default Description name str required Component identifier string. backend FluidBackend required Fluid property backend.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Name Direction Type Description inl Inlet FluidPort Two-phase entry stream (\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} > 0\)). vap Outlet FluidPort Saturated vapor discharge stream (\(\dot{m}_{\text{vap}} < 0\), \(x = 1.0\)). liq Outlet FluidPort Saturated liquid drain stream (\(\dot{m}_{\text{liq}} < 0\), \(x = 0.0\)).

docs.title: Governing Equations & Residuals
docs.text:
The component contributes 6 algebraic residuals (residuals()):

  1. Mass conservation ("mass"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{vap}} + \dot{m}_{\text{liq}} = 0\)$
  2. Energy conservation ("energy"): $\(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} h_{\text{inl}} + \dot{m}_{\text{vap}} h_g(p_{\text{inl}}) + \dot{m}_{\text{liq}} h_f(p_{\text{inl}}) = 0\)$
  3. Vapor outlet saturation ("sat_vapour"): $\(h_{\text{vap}} - h_g(p_{\text{inl}}) = 0\)$
  4. Liquid outlet saturation ("sat_liquid"): $\(h_{\text{liq}} - h_f(p_{\text{inl}}) = 0\)$
  5. Vapor pressure equilibrium ("p_vap"): $\(p_{\text{vap}} - p_{\text{inl}} = 0\)$
  6. Liquid pressure equilibrium ("p_liq"): $\(p_{\text{liq}} - p_{\text{inl}} = 0\)$

where \(h_g(p) = \text{backend.h\_pq}(p, 1.0)\) and \(h_f(p) = \text{backend.h\_pq}(p, 0.0)\).

docs.title: Post-Solve Outputs
docs.text: • flash.vapour_fraction: Dryness / separated vapor fraction: $\(x_{\text{sep}} = \frac{-\dot{m}_{\text{vap}}}{\dot{m}_{\text{inl}}}\)$

docs.title: Pre-Solve Sanity Checks (_own_start_sanity)
docs.text:
• \(\dot{m}_{\text{inl}} > 0\) (must be an inflow).
  • \(\dot{m}_{\text{vap}} < 0\) and \(\dot{m}_{\text{liq}} < 0\) (must be outflows).

docs.title: Fluid Backends & Properties
docs.text: All thermophysical and transport properties in Caldis are managed through backends implementing caldis.fluids.backend.FluidBackend.

docs.title: CoolPropBackend
docs.text:
caldis.fluids.coolprop_backend.CoolPropBackend wraps CoolProp's high-accuracy Helmholtz equations of state.

from caldis.fluids import CoolPropBackend

# Initialize pure or pseudo-pure fluids
air = CoolPropBackend("Air")
water = CoolPropBackend("Water")
r134a = CoolPropBackend("R134a")
co2 = CoolPropBackend("CO2")

docs.title: State & Thermodynamic Evaluation
docs.text:
All primary state evaluations take \((p, h)\) as input coordinates:

Method Description Units Notes T(p, h) Temperature \(\text{K}\) Valid in single-phase and two-phase. rho(p, h) Mass density \(\text{kg/m}^3\) Mixture density under the dome. quality(p, h) Vapor quality \(x\) \(-\) \(0 \le x \le 1\) in two-phase; -1.0 if subcooled liquid; 2.0 if superheated vapor. s(p, h) Specific entropy \(\text{J/kg/K}\) Reference state depends on CoolProp convention. h_ps(p, s) Isentropic enthalpy \(\text{J/kg}\) Used for ideal turbine/compressor expansions. h_pt(p, T) Enthalpy from \((p, T)\) \(\text{J/kg}\) Used for seeding starts or boundary conversions. h_pq(p, Q) Saturation enthalpy \(\text{J/kg}\) \(Q=0\) (bubble point \(h_f\)), \(Q=1\) (dew point \(h_g\)). default_state(T_hint) Universal start point (p, h) Returns \((10^5 \text{ Pa}, h(10^5, T_{\text{hint}}))\).

docs.title: Transport & Thermal Properties
docs.text: Method Description Units mu(p, h) Dynamic viscosity \(\text{Pa}\cdot\text{s}\) cond(p, h) Thermal conductivity \(\text{W/m/K}\) cp(p, h) Specific heat capacity \(c_p\) \(\text{J/kg/K}\) Pr(p, h) Prandtl number \(-\) sigma(p, h) Surface tension \(\text{N/m}\)

docs.title: Abstract Interface (FluidBackend)
docs.text: To implement custom fluid models (e.g. ideal gases or tabulated bicubic splines), subclass FluidBackend and implement T, rho, and quality.

docs.title: Dynamic DAE Simulation
docs.text: In addition to steady-state cycle analysis, Caldis features a native differential-algebraic equation (DAE) simulator: caldis.solvers.simulate.

docs.title: Index-1 DAE Formulation
docs.text:
A dynamic model in Caldis combines: - Differential equations: \(\dot{x}_d = f(x_d, x_a, t)\) for accumulated quantities (mass \(M\), internal energy \(U\), wall temperature \(T_{\text{wall}}\)). - Algebraic constraints: \(0 = g(x_d, x_a, t)\) for instantaneous balances (momentum, valve flow laws, algebraic port connections).

The integrated system solves the implicit residual form:

\[F(\dot{x}_d, x_d, x_a, t) = 0\]

Using an implicit backward differentiation (BDF / implicit Euler) scheme:

\[\dot{x}_{d, k+1} \approx \frac{x_{d, k+1} - x_{d, k}}{\Delta t}\]

docs.title: Canonical Dynamic Model: Heated Storage Tank
docs.text: A standard application is a dynamic fluid tank with internal energy and wall thermal capacitance:

docs.title: The Simulation Workflow
docs.text:
from caldis.solvers import simulate

# Run dynamic simulation for 60 seconds with 0.5 s timestep
results = simulate(
    sys,
    t_end=60.0,
    dt=0.5,
    init="steady",             # or "current"
    update_inputs=my_input_fn, # optional time-dependent forcing
    progress=True
)

docs.title: Initial State (init)
docs.text:
• init="steady": Solves a steady-state problem at \(t = 0\) with all differential derivatives set to zero (\(\dot{x}_d = 0\)), providing physically consistent initial algebraic states.
  • init="current": Uses _consistent_init() to hold differential states fixed at their current initial conditions while resolving the algebraic variables to satisfy all residuals.

docs.title: Dynamic Input Driving (update_inputs)
docs.text:
To drive the simulation with time-varying parameters (e.g., ramping thermal duty, closing a valve):

def update_inputs(system, t):
    # Ramp heater power from 1 kW to 5 kW over 30 seconds
    if t < 30.0:
        heater.params["Qdot"] = 1000.0 + (4000.0 / 30.0) * t
    else:
        heater.params["Qdot"] = 5000.0

docs.title: Navigating Results (Results)
docs.text:
The returned results object provides hierarchical attribute navigation over the simulation history:

# Access time vector
t = results.time

# Access nested variables
T_wall = results.tank.wall.T        # NumPy 1D array of length N
p_fluid = results.tank.fluid.p

# Port access (with Python keyword handling)
m_in = results.tank.fluid["in"].mdot

# Convert entire history to pandas DataFrame
df = results.to_dataframe()

docs.title: Second-Law Exergy Analysis
docs.text: First-law energy balances track energy quantity but ignore energy degradation and irreversibility. Caldis provides built-in second-law exergy analysis at both component and system levels.

docs.title: The Dead State \((T_0, p_0)\)
docs.text:
All physical exergy flows are evaluated relative to an ambient reference (dead) state:

\[e = (h - h_0) - T_0 (s - s_0)\] \[\dot{X} = \dot{m} \cdot e\]

Where \(h_0\) and \(s_0\) are the specific enthalpy and entropy evaluated at \((p_0, T_0)\).

docs.title: Generating an Exergy Report
docs.text:
# 1. Solve the system
sol = solve(sys)

# 2. Set the ambient dead state (e.g. 15 °C, 1.01325 bar)
sys.set_reference(T_ref=288.15, p_ref=101325.0)

# 3. Generate exergy report
exergy_df = sys.exergy_report(as_dataframe=True)
print(exergy_df)

docs.title: Report Columns
docs.text: Column Definition Description X_supplied Exergy consumed (\(\text{W}\)) Shaft work input or fuel exergy provided to component. X_recovered Exergy produced (\(\text{W}\)) Useful exergy transferred into stream or shaft power output. X_destroyed Exergy destruction \(\dot{X}_d\) (\(\text{W}\)) Irreversibility: \(\dot{X}_d = T_0 \dot{S}_{\text{gen}} = X_{\text{supplied}} - X_{\text{recovered}}\). eta_II Exergetic efficiency \(\eta_{\text{II}}\) \(\eta_{\text{II}} = \frac{X_{\text{recovered}}}{X_{\text{supplied}}}\).

docs.title: Turbines & Compressors
docs.text:
Turbine:

\[X_{\text{supplied}} = \dot{m} (e_{\text{in}} - e_{\text{out}}), \quad X_{\text{recovered}} = \dot{W}_{\text{shaft}}\]

Compressor:

\[X_{\text{supplied}} = |\dot{W}_{\text{shaft}}|, \quad X_{\text{recovered}} = \dot{m} (e_{\text{out}} - e_{\text{in}})\]

docs.title: Expansion Valves
docs.text:
Valves are purely dissipative devices:

\[X_{\text{recovered}} = 0, \quad X_{\text{destroyed}} = T_0 \dot{S}_{\text{gen}} = \dot{m} T_0 (s_{\text{out}} - s_{\text{in}})\]

docs.title: Heat Exchangers & Heaters
docs.text: For SimpleHeater, the user must provide T_source (the temperature of the heat source/sink reservoir). For electric resistance heating, set T_source = float('inf').

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Document Type: Tutorial

This is a step-by-step learning guide designed to lead a newcomer through building, configuring, and solving their first thermodynamic system in Caldis.

docs.title: What You'll Learn
docs.text:
In this tutorial, you will:

  1. Install Caldis and its underlying thermodynamic property libraries.
  2. Initialize fluid backends with CoolProp.
  3. Build and connect a 4-component open air compression and cooling loop.
  4. Close degrees of freedom using fix_port.
  5. Seed initial guesses with autostart and compute the solution.

docs.title: Prerequisites & Installation
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have Python 3.10+ installed. Install Caldis along with the required scientific computing and thermodynamic packages:

pip install coolprop numpy scipy pandas
pip install -e .

docs.title: The Workflow
docs.text: We will model a continuous air compression and cooling process:

docs.title: 1. Imports and Backend Initialization
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from caldis.core.system import System
from caldis.components import FluidBoundary, Compressor, SimpleHeater
from caldis.fluids import CoolPropBackend
from caldis.solvers import solve
from caldis.solvers.autostart import fix_port, autostart

# Use CoolProp for air thermophysical properties
air = CoolPropBackend("Air")

docs.title: 2. Define Components & Connect
docs.text:
p_suction = 1.0e5       # 1 bar
T_suction = 288.15      # 15 °C
mass_flow = 2.5         # 2.5 kg/s

# 1. Source (imposes p, T, mdot)
# Note: mass flow is negative because it leaves the source
src = FluidBoundary("src", p=p_suction, T=T_suction, mdot=-mass_flow, backend=air)

# 2. Compressor (isentropic efficiency 0.85)
comp = Compressor("comp", backend=air, eta_is=0.85)

# 3. Cooler (duty Qdot=None: closed by imposing downstream temperature)
cooler = SimpleHeater("cooler", backend=air, Qdot=None, dp=0.0)

# 4. Sink (unconstrained boundary)
sink = FluidBoundary("sink", backend=air)

# Build system and connect ports
sys = System("compression_test")
sys.add(src, comp, cooler, sink)

sys.connect(src.port, comp.inl)
sys.connect(comp.out, cooler.inl)
sys.connect(cooler.out, sink.port)

docs.title: 3. Impose Design Specifications (fix_port)
docs.text:
At this stage, the system has 2 degrees of freedom: 1. The compressor discharge pressure is unconstrained. 2. The cooler duty is unconstrained.

We close both using fix_port:

p_discharge = 6.0e5     # 6 bar
T_target = 303.15       # 30 °C

fix_port(sys, comp.out, p=p_discharge)
fix_port(sys, cooler.out, T=T_target)

docs.title: 4. Seed and Solve
docs.text:
# 1. Propagate start values automatically
autostart(sys, verbose=True)

# 2. Run solver (preflight checks DOF -> direct Newton -> homotopy fallback)
sol = solve(sys, verbose=True)

if sol.success:
    print("\n--- RESULTS ---")
    print(f"Compressor Work (absorbed): {comp.Wdot / 1e3:.2f} kW")
    print(f"Compressor Discharge Temp:  {comp.out.T - 273.15:.1f} °C")
    print(f"Cooler Duty (extracted):    {cooler.Qdot / 1e3:.2f} kW")
    print(f"Pressure Ratio:             {comp.pressure_ratio:.2f}")

docs.title: Tabulating Port States
docs.text:
Caldis provides sys.port_table() to format every fluid port into a structured table or Pandas DataFrame:

df = sys.port_table()
print(df[["p_bar", "T_C", "h_kJkg", "mdot"]])

docs.title: Closing Closed-Loop Cycles
docs.text:
In open-loop architectures, mass flow enters via a source and exits through a sink. In closed thermodynamic loops (e.g., closed Brayton gas cycles, vapor-compression heat pumps, ORC loops), fluid recirculates indefinitely.

This introduces a fundamental topological issue: redundant mass conservation.

docs.title: The Closed-Loop Redundancy Problem
docs.text:
Consider a simple closed loop connecting four components in series:

\[A \longrightarrow B \longrightarrow C \longrightarrow D \longrightarrow A\]

Every standard connection adds 3 equations: 1. \(p_a = p_b\) 2. \(h_a = h_b\) 3. \(\dot{m}_a + \dot{m}_b = 0\)

Summing mass equations along the loop yields:

\[(\dot{m}_{A,\text{out}} + \dot{m}_{B,\text{in}}) + (\dot{m}_{B,\text{out}} + \dot{m}_{C,\text{in}}) + \dots = 0\]

Because each component already satisfies \(\dot{m}_{\text{in}} + \dot{m}_{\text{out}} = 0\), the \(N\)-th mass connection equation is a linear combination of all preceding mass balances.

If all connections enforce mass conservation, the system will be over-specified (\(\text{DOF} = -1\)), causing a rank-deficient Jacobian.

docs.title: The Solution: close_loop=True
docs.text:
When wiring the final connection that closes the loop, specify close_loop=True:

# Standard connections:
sys.connect(comp.out, heater.inl)
sys.connect(heater.out, turb.inl)
sys.connect(turb.out, cooler.inl)

# CLOSING CONNECTION:
sys.connect(cooler.out, comp.inl, close_loop=True)

docs.title: What close_loop=True Does:
docs.text:
• Enforces pressure continuity: \(p_{\text{cooler,out}} - p_{\text{comp,inl}} = 0\)
  • Enforces enthalpy continuity: \(h_{\text{cooler,out}} - h_{\text{comp,inl}} = 0\)
  • Drops the redundant mass balance equation: \(\dot{m}\) is left to be determined by the cycle boundary conditions (e.g., total inventory, specified flow rate, or component characteristic curve).

docs.title: Example: Vapor-Compression Heat Pump Cycle
docs.text: A canonical closed cycle is the 4-component vapor-compression heat pump:

docs.title: Setting Mass Flow in a Closed Loop
docs.text: Because no source imposes flow, you must provide one condition that fixes the flow rate or mass inventory:

docs.title: Approach A: Fix Flow Rate on a Machine or Valve
docs.text:
# Fix mass flow rate directly on the compressor inlet
fix_port(sys, comp.inl, mdot=5.0)

docs.title: Approach B: Fixed Charge / Accumulator
docs.text: If an accumulator or variable-volume tank is included, the loop pressure and mass distribution adjust dynamically to match the inventory.

docs.title: Autostart Engine Reference
docs.text: The autostart engine (caldis.solvers.autostart) handles start-point seeding without requiring manual initial guesses for every port.

docs.title: autostart(sys, T_default=283.15, verbose=False)
docs.text:
Executes multi-level propagation over the system: 1. Level 1: Initializes every port to safe fluid defaults (default_state(T_default)). 2. Level 2: Iteratively fires direction-agnostic propagation rules from high-provenance nodes (BOUNDARY, HINT) down into unassigned DEFAULT ports. 3. Level 3: Seeds internal variables (e.g. cell profiles in HXSim).

from caldis.solvers.autostart import autostart

autostart(sys, verbose=True)

docs.title: fix_port(system, port, p=None, T=None, h=None, mdot=None)
docs.text:
Simultaneously adds a system-level constraint and seeds the port start value with BOUNDARY provenance.

from caldis.solvers.autostart import fix_port

# Impose pressure constraint and seed start value
fix_port(sys, comp.out, p=8.0e5)

# Impose temperature constraint (converts to h via port backend)
fix_port(sys, hex.cold_out, T=320.0)

docs.title: When to Add Manual Hints
docs.text:
While autostart handles linear pressure drops and flow propagation across series components, highly nonlinear machines (turbines, compressors) or complex counterflow heat exchangers may need an explicit hint:

# Provide an expected discharge temperature for the compressor:
sys.set_start_port(comp.out, T=450.0)

# Set high/low pressure sides of a heat exchanger:
sys.set_start(recuperator, p=10e5, side="cold")
sys.set_start(recuperator, p=1.2e5, side="hot")

docs.title: Dynamic Integrator Reference
docs.text: The dynamic solver caldis.solvers.dynamic.simulate integrates systems containing differential state variables over time.

docs.title: Function Signature
docs.text:
def simulate(
    system,
    t_end,
    dt,
    update_inputs=None,
    init="steady",
    tol=1e-8,
    progress=False
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• system (System): The assembled Caldis system.
  • t_end (float): End time of the simulation in seconds (\(s\)).
  • dt (float): Time integration step size (\(s\)).
  • update_inputs (callable or None): Function of signature fn(system, t) invoked at each timestep to apply dynamic boundary conditions, disturbances, or control signals.
  • init (str):
  • "steady" (default): Runs an initial steady solve (\(\dot{x} = 0\)) at \(t = 0\).
  • "current": Preserves existing state values and performs consistent initialization on algebraic variables using _consistent_init.
  • tol (float): Newton solver convergence tolerance at each time step.
  • progress (bool): Displays simulation progress bar.

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: Returns an instance of caldis.experiments.results.Results.

docs.title: Consistent Initialization at \(t = 0\)
docs.text:
Differential-algebraic systems cannot accept arbitrary initial conditions for algebraic variables. If a user sets \(M_0\) and \(U_0\) in a tank, the initial pressure \(p_0\), enthalpy \(h_0\), and flow rates must satisfy all component balance laws.

_consistent_init(system, states, tol):

  1. Pins all differential variables to their initial condition: \(x_d - x_{d, 0} = 0\).
  2. Leaves time derivatives \(\dot{x}_d\) free as algebraic unknowns.

  3. Solves the combined system:

    \[\begin{pmatrix} F(x_d, x_a, \dot{x}_d, t=0) \\ x_d - x_{d, 0} \end{pmatrix} = 0\]

    ensuring that recorded history at \(t = 0\) is physically consistent.

docs.title: Steady-State Solvers & Homotopy Continuation
docs.text: Caldis solves nonlinear algebraic systems \(F(x) = 0\) using a multi-stage approach combining damped Newton methods and parameter continuation.

docs.title: The Unified solve() Function
docs.text:
from caldis.solvers import solve

sol = solve(
    system,
    steps=3,
    verbose=True,
    show_homotopy=False,
    diagnostics=True,
    raise_on_fail=False,
    strict_physical=False,
    try_newton_first=True
)

docs.title: 1. Damped Global Newton (newton)
docs.text: The direct solver uses a bounded, scaled damped Newton algorithm: - Evaluates the Jacobian \(J\) via finite differences normalized by each variable's characteristic scale. - Solves \(J \Delta x = -F(x)\). - Performs backtracking line search to ensure reduction of residual norm \(\|F(x)\|\). - Enforces variable lower and upper bounds (v.lower, v.upper).

docs.title: 2. Homotopy Continuation (solve_homotopy)
docs.text:
When direct Newton fails due to highly nonlinear start points, Caldis falls back to homotopy continuation:

\[H(x, \lambda) = F(x) - (1 - \lambda) F(x_0) = 0, \quad \lambda \in [0, 1]\]
  • At \(\lambda = 0\): \(H(x_0, 0) = 0\) is trivially satisfied by the initial guess \(x_0\).
  • The continuation parameter \(\lambda\) is stepped from \(0 \rightarrow 1\) across \(N\) steps (steps=3 by default).
  • Each step uses the solution of the previous step as its starting point.
  • At \(\lambda = 1\): \(H(x, 1) = F(x) = 0\), recovering the true solution.

docs.title: Post-Solve Physical Verification
docs.text:
A solution can converge mathematically while being physically impossible (e.g., negative temperature approaches where heat flows from cold to hot).

After convergence, solve() runs system.physical_check(). - If violations exist (such as temperature crossings), warnings are printed. - If strict_physical=True, sol.success is flipped to False.

docs.title: Diagnostic Tools Reference
docs.text: Caldis includes built-in diagnostic tools (caldis.core.diagnostics) to inspect system health, conditioning, and convergence failure points.

docs.title: 1. Jacobian Structure Report (jacobian_report)
docs.text:
from caldis.core.diagnostics import jacobian_report

jacobian_report(system, top=6)

Evaluates the finite-difference Jacobian at the current state \(x\), balancing rows by residual magnitude and columns by variable scale.

docs.title: Output Insights
docs.text:
• Full Rank: Confirms the linear system is regular and nonsingular.
  • Rank Deficient: Computes the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD):
  • Right null vector: Lists specific variables that have lost sensitivity and need start re-anchoring.
  • Left null vector: Lists the redundant or unconstrained equations.

docs.title: 2. Convergence Report (convergence_report)
docs.text:
from caldis.core.diagnostics import convergence_report

convergence_report(system, sol, top=8)

Post-mortem analyzer invoked automatically when solve() fails. - Ranks residuals by scaled violation magnitude (normalizing units so mass balances and energy balances are directly comparable). - Dissects connection mismatches (e.g., showing exact pressure or enthalpy discrepancies across connected ports). - Identifies any variables stuck against their lower or upper bounds (v.lower, v.upper).

docs.title: Print Component Hierarchy
docs.text:
sys.structure()
Recursively displays the tree of components, child sub-components, ports, and internal variables.

docs.title: Pre-solve Sanity Check
docs.text:
sys.check_start_sanity(verbose=True)
Evaluates all component-level physical sanity checks against \(x_0\) before attempting a solve.

docs.title: Common Errors & Troubleshooting
docs.text: A guide to diagnosing and fixing the most frequent modeling and numerical errors in Caldis.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text: ValueError: [DOF sous-spécifié] 14 inconnues, 12 équations : il manque 2 condition(s) aux limites (variables non déterminées).

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The system has more unknowns than equations. Some boundary pressures, temperatures, or design targets are missing.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Use fix_port or add a FluidBoundary spec to close the missing degrees of freedom. Common culprits: - A compressor or turbine without a specified outlet pressure or pressure ratio. - A heat exchanger or heater without a specified duty or target temperature. - An unconstrained recirculating mass flow in a closed cycle.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text: ValueError: [DOF sur-spécifié] 12 inconnues, 13 équations : 1 équation(s) de trop (condition imposée en double ?).

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: More equations exist than unknowns.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• Check if you wired a closed loop without setting close_loop=True on the final connection.
  • Check if both pressure and temperature are imposed on both ends of a component with fixed pressure drop.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
ValueError: Start point not evaluable:
  - component hex: residual[4] is non-finite (value=nan)

docs.title: Cause

docs.title: Solution
